surprises.head: Dallas leaned on their bottom six
surprises.body: Dallas rides their top six more than most teams. Not tonight: the bottom six played 46% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 41% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 150 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: A natural hat trick for Robertson
paras: The Capitals almost pulled off something wild. Joel Kiviranta got the scoring started for the Stars midway through the first. There were seven goals in the second period alone. Jason Robertson made it 2-0 on the power play just 23 seconds into the period. The Stars’ Miro Heiskanen left early in the period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day. Robertson scored his second of the night early in the period to make it 3-0 for the Stars. Robertson completed a natural hat trick two and a half minutes later to make it 4-0. Washington pulled Logan Thompson after four goals and turned to Charlie Lindgren for the rest of the second. Jordan Kyrou got the Caps on the board on the power play midway through the second. Mikko Rantanen made it 5-1 for the Stars just under four minutes later, his 800th NHL point. Boone Jenner and Jakob Chychrun scored two and a half minutes apart late in the second to cut Dallas’ lead to 5-3. Roope Hintz stretched the lead to 6-3 early in the third, and that goal turned out to be the winner. Justin Sourdif made it 6-4 with just over seven minutes left. With the goalie pulled and just over a minute left, Ryan Leonard pulled the Capitals within one, but the Stars held on. Hintz and Kyrou each had a goal and two assists.

The Stars had a bit more of the good stuff. Jake Oettinger made 20 saves for the Stars. The Stars moved to 9-5-1 and climbed to third in the Central, while the Capitals fell to 8-6-0, slipping to fourth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Roope Hintz extended his point streak against Washington to six games.
The Stars have beaten the Capitals four straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
Jakob Chychrun scored for the first time in twelve games.
